chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man performs khul' (divorce by redemption) with his wife, she becomes a single, independent woman, and he is a suitor among suitors. It is not permissible for him to take back what he gave until she is the one who requests that from him, without him harming her, and until she says: 'I will not give you a full share of my dowry, nor will I bathe for you from ritual impurity, and I will surely bring into your house someone you dislike, and I will make your bed shared [with another], and I will not uphold God's boundaries upon you.' When this is from her, then what he took from her is pleasing to him [i.e., the khul' is valid]."

key_terms.خَاطِبٌ: Suitor (husband's status after khul', needing to re-court)
key_terms.خَلَعَ: Khul' (divorce by redemption where the wife pays compensation)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions required for a husband to validly reclaim the khul' payment from his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential mechanics of *khul'*, emphasizing that the husband retains the right to reclaim the redemption payment only if the wife initiates the separation and provides valid grounds, such as irreconcilable differences or specific grievances. It underscores the Shia principle that *khul'* is not merely a financial transaction but a consensual dissolution where the wife's active request validates the husband's retention of the consideration, preventing unilateral exploitation.
